title: Find out why main’s checks sometimes see a title’s words as not drawn, then pass on the same code
goal: Three times in a day main’s tests went red on CI because a check that looks at drawn words found them missing: twice the title entrance check saw most of a title’s words off screen, and once the legibility check read a dark caption preview as grey text on the same grey. Each time the next run on the same app code passed, and the tests pass on this Mac. Find out whether the words really are sometimes drawn late or blank on a busy machine, or the checks look too early, and fix whichever it is so main stays green.
notes: CI run https://github.com/dzearing/photonz/actions/runs/43367299841 (commit 610f1dc95), Test slice 1 of 3, step Run tests, after all 5535 tests passed: 'legibility: 1546 words and icons measured on 122 specimens, light and dark, in 43s' then 'legibility: UNREADABLE (the user: no white on white or black on black, ever): Caption preview, Lower third, still, dark: 1.00:1, #232323 on #232323, at 10,10 (caption-preview-lower-third-still-dark.png)' and exit 1. The next CI run, 43368952566 on b20245458 (a queue-only commit, same app code), passed. Not reproduced locally; the check lives in Scripts/test.sh (grep photonz-legibility). Filed by a-long-reference-edit-opens-in-the-probe-in-one, which does not touch captions. Epic is video-perf only because the queue requires a now-staged epic; it is a test-health item.
acceptance: The cause is named with evidence for both checks: a reproduction of the missing words (for example the suite run under load, or on a CI runner), or the check’s timing shown to be the cause.
Whichever it is is fixed, and TextRevealUnclippedTests and the legibility check on the caption previews each pass 10 runs in a row under the same parallel load CI uses (Scripts/test.sh --shard K/3).
If the cause is in the app (words drawn blank when the machine is busy), a person playing or exporting a title never sees a frame with its words missing, and a test holds that.
